question: Who suggested that the origin of life must have been from simple inorganic substances?
solution:
The correct answer is __**JBS Haldane**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **JBS Haldane** suggested that the origin of life must have been from simple inorganic substances.
 
• Haldane, along with Alexander Oparin, independently proposed the hypothesis of the "**primordial soup**" where life began in a warm pond with a mix of chemicals.
 
• His ideas contributed significantly to the field of abiogenesis, the study of how life on Earth could have arisen from inanimate matter.
 
• This hypothesis laid the foundation for future experimental work, such as the Miller-Urey experiment, which tested the chemical origins of life.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **JBS Haldane** was a British-born Indian scientist known for his works in physiology, genetics, evolutionary biology, and mathematics.
 
• He was one of the founders of the field of population genetics.
 
• Haldane's work in evolutionary biology and genetics helped bridge the gap between Darwinian evolution and Mendelian genetics.
 
• He proposed that the early Earth's atmosphere was reducing, which was essential for the chemical reactions that led to the formation of organic molecules.
